## What app.honcho.dev Is

The URL app.honcho.dev is the **login and dashboard portal** for Honcho, a memory infrastructure platform for building stateful AI agents. It offers sign-in via Google, GitHub, email/password, or magic link, and a "Create Account" option for new users.[1]

## What Honcho Does

Honcho is an open-source memory library (with a managed cloud service) designed to help AI agents build and maintain persistent, evolving understanding of "peers" — users, other agents, groups, projects, and ideas — over time. Rather than resetting context every session, it lets developers store messages and events, then have Honcho reason on them in the background so agents can query peer representations, session context, search results, or natural-language insights from any LLM or framework. The project's tagline positions it for use cases like AI companions where "relationships deepen, not reset".[2][3][4]

## Getting Started on the Platform

When you sign up at app.honcho.dev, you're prompted to join (or create) an organization, which receives its own dedicated Honcho instance plus **$100 in free credits**. From there, the dashboard exposes:[3][5]

- **API Keys** page — generate keys needed to call the Honcho API[5]
- **API Playground** (app.honcho.dev/playground) — test queries and explore endpoints in-browser without writing code[6]
- **Webhooks** page — configure real-time event notifications (message delivery, session updates, peer state changes) via HTTP POST[6]
- **Members** page — manage organization/team access and admin permissions[6]

## Pricing and Self-Hosting

The managed service charges for ingestion (storing + background "Neuromancer" reasoning) at **$2.00 per million tokens**, offers an unlimited, ~200ms `context()` call for retrieving curated state, and tiered query pricing ($0.001/query for basic conclusions, up to $0.50/query for deeper ones). If you'd rather not use the hosted service, Honcho is open-source (github.com/plastic-labs/honcho) and can be self-hosted via Docker or manually with PostgreSQL + pgvector, pointing the Python/TypeScript SDKs at your own `localhost:8000` instance instead of `api.honcho.dev`.[4][7][3]
